_meta.indication: For the treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) in adults and in pediatric patients 2 years and older.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 (recommended Phase 2 dose 12 µg/kg/day x 5 days of a 21-day cycle)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with treatment-naïve BPDCN (pivotal cohort of 13 patients) and 15 patients with relapsed or refractory BPDCN
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of complete response or clinical complete response (CR/CRc)
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment-naïve BPDCN: CR/CRc rate 7/13 = 53.8% (95% CI 25.1, 80.8); median duration of CR/CRc not reached. In relapsed/refractory BPDCN, one patient achieved a CR (duration 111 days) and one a CRc (duration 424 days).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥30%): capillary leak syndrome, nausea, fatigue, peripheral edema, pyrexia and weight increase. Overall incidence of CLS was 55% (52/94) including Grade 3 in 6%, Grade 4 in 1% and 2 fatal events (2%). Ten (11%) patients discontinued treatment due to an adverse reaction.
target_moa: A CD123-directed cytotoxin: a recombinant human IL-3 fused to a truncated diphtheria toxin; the IL-3 domain targets IL-3R (CD123)-expressing BPDCN cells, ultimately inactivating cellular protein synthesis leading to apoptosis.
modality: Other (recombinant IL-3 / truncated diphtheria toxin immunotoxin fusion protein)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: CAPILLARY LEAK SYNDROME — Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS), which may be life-threatening or fatal if not properly managed, can occur in patients receiving ELZONRIS.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

The Midcycle Communication was held on 10/3/2018, and the Late Cycle Meeting was held on 11/15/2018.

summary.text: Tagraxofusp-erzs (Elzonris) received orphan drug designation (6/6/2013) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (8/22/2016) for BPDCN, was submitted as a rolling BLA (final part received 6/21/2018), reviewed under Priority review, and granted regular (not accelerated) approval on 12/21/2018 based on the CR/CRc rate with durability in the single-arm Phase 2 study STML-401-0114.

citations.quote: Orphan Designation for treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm was granted on 6/6/2013, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm was granted on 8/22/2016.
The BLA was filed 60 days thereafter with a Priority review classification.
The benefit-risk assessment supports regular approval of tagraxofusp-erzs for the treatment of BPDCN in adult and pediatric patients 2 years and older.
